title: Unit 1: The First 4 Consonants
subtitle: Hangul Baby Steps
description: Meet the simplest building blocks of Korean: ㄱ, ㄴ, ㄷ, ㄹ.

lessons.title: Meet ㄱ (Giyeok) & ㄴ (Nieun)
lessons.introduction: Korean letters look like pictures of sounds! Let's meet your very first two letters.

cards.mnemonic: Looks like an elbow or a corner. Makes a soft 'g' sound as in 'go'.
Looks like the side of a Nose! Makes the 'n' sound as in 'nest'.

storyPages.text: Baby Bear found a wooden corner stick shaped like 'ㄱ' in the forest.
A tiny butterfly landed right on his Nose, which looked like 'ㄴ'!
Now Baby Bear remembers: Corner is 'ㄱ' (g) and Nose is 'ㄴ' (n)!

lessons.title: Meet ㄷ (Digeut) & ㄹ (Rieul)
lessons.introduction: You mastered ㄱ and ㄴ! Now let's meet two friendly steps forward: ㄷ and ㄹ.

cards.mnemonic: Looks like an open Doorway! Makes the 'd' sound as in 'door'.
Curvy like a winding Road or snake! Makes an 'r' / 'l' sound.

story.title: The Door and the Winding Road

storyPages.text: Baby Bear opened the Door 'ㄷ' to start his morning adventure.
He walked down the winding Road 'ㄹ' toward the sparkling river.

questions.prompt: Which letter looks like a Nose and sounds like 'n'?
questions.explanation: ㄴ represents the tongue touching the roof of mouth, shaped like a Nose ('n').

questions.prompt: Listen to the sound and choose the matching Korean consonant:
questions.explanation: You heard '그' (g) which is ㄱ (Giyeok)!

questions.prompt: Which letter looks like an open Door ('d')?
questions.explanation: ㄷ is shaped like a Door and produces the 'd' sound.

questions.prompt: What sound does ㄹ (winding road) make?
questions.explanation: ㄹ sounds like a light flap 'r' or 'l'.

questions.prompt: Trace the letter ㄱ with your finger on the screen!
options: Trace ㄱ with your finger to complete!
questions.explanation: Super job! ㄱ is a top horizontal stroke followed by a vertical drop.

questions.prompt: Listen carefully. Which consonant matches this sound?
questions.explanation: You heard the '드' (d) sound, which is ㄷ (Digeut - Door)!

questions.prompt: Listen to the audio. Which letter corresponds to this sound?
questions.explanation: You heard the '느' (n) sound, which corresponds to ㄴ (Nieun - Nose)!

questions.prompt: Which consonant is shaped like a corner or gun, representing the back of the tongue?
questions.explanation: ㄱ (Giyeok) represents the tongue blocking the throat at a 90-degree corner!

questions.prompt: In the word '고양이' (Goyang-i - Cat), what is the starting consonant sound?
questions.explanation: 고양이 begins with 'ㄱ', making the soft 'g' sound!

questions.prompt: Which letter represents a winding road or rattlesnake?
questions.explanation: ㄹ (Rieul) has a zig-zag snake or winding road shape!

questions.prompt: Match the word '나비' (Nabi - Butterfly) with its starting letter:
questions.explanation: 나비 (Butterfly) starts with 'ㄴ' (n)!

questions.prompt: Trace the letter ㄴ (Nieun) with your finger on the screen!
questions.explanation: Awesome! ㄴ starts from the top vertical stroke and turns right horizontally.

questions.prompt: Trace the letter ㄷ (Digeut) with your finger on the screen!
questions.explanation: Great work! ㄷ is drawn with a top horizontal stroke, then an L-shaped base.

questions.prompt: Which consonant starts the Korean word '다람쥐' (Daramjwi - Squirrel)?
questions.explanation: 다람쥐 begins with ㄷ (d)!

title: Unit 2: Basic Vowels (ㅏ, ㅓ, ㅗ, ㅜ, ㅡ, ㅣ)
subtitle: Breathing Life with Vowels
description: Consonants need vowels to speak! Learn the 6 foundational Korean vowel sounds.

lessons.title: Bright Vowels: ㅏ (a) & ㅗ (o)
lessons.introduction: Vowels are made of the Sky (•), Earth (ㅡ), and Person (ㅣ).

cards.mnemonic: A person pointing right towards the bright sun: 'Ah!'.
The sun rising above the horizon line: 'Oh! sunrise!'.

storyPages.text: The sun pops up above the earth: 'ㅗ' (o)!
Baby Bear smiles and shouts: 'ㅏ' (a)!

lessons.title: Cozy Vowels: ㅓ (eo) & ㅜ (u)
lessons.introduction: Now let's flip the direction! When strokes point left or down, they make deeper, cozy sounds.

cards.mnemonic: Points LEFT (inward). Imagine someone bumping into you and saying 'Uh-oh!' (eo).
Points DOWN below the earth line like tree roots: 'Oo!' as in 'moon'.

storyPages.text: When the sun hides, Baby Bear looks back toward his mother: 'ㅓ' (eo - uh)!
He drinks warm milk under the moonlight: 'ㅜ' (u - oo)!

lessons.title: Earth & Sky Person: ㅡ (eu) & ㅣ (i)
lessons.introduction: Meet the two purest shapes in Korean: the flat Earth (ㅡ) and the standing Person (ㅣ)!

cards.mnemonic: A flat horizontal line like the ground! Smile wide and pull your lips flat: 'eu' (like 'put' without rounding lips).
Stands tall like a Person or the number 1! Sounds like 'ee' in 'tree'.

storyPages.text: Baby Bear lies flat on the soft forest ground: 'ㅡ' (eu)!
Then he stands up straight and tall like a person: 'ㅣ' (i - ee)!

questions.prompt: Which vowel sounds like 'ah' in 'father'?
questions.explanation: ㅏ produces the open 'ah' sound!

questions.prompt: Which vowel represents the sun rising ABOVE the horizon line?
questions.explanation: ㅗ represents the bright sun pointing upward above the earth horizon ('o')!

questions.prompt: Listen to the vowel sound and choose the correct letter:
questions.explanation: You heard '오' (o) as in 'open' or 'boat', which is ㅗ!

questions.prompt: Which vowel has a horizontal ground with a vertical line pointing DOWN under the earth?
questions.explanation: ㅜ points downward beneath the horizon, making the 'oo' sound as in 'moon'!

questions.prompt: Listen carefully. Which vowel matches this sound?
questions.explanation: You heard the open '아' (ah) sound, which is ㅏ!

questions.prompt: What sound does the vowel ㅓ make?
questions.explanation: ㅓ has an inward stroke pointing left, sounding like 'eo' or 'uh' as in 'sun'!

questions.prompt: In Korean vowel philosophy, what does the vertical standing line (ㅣ) represent?
questions.explanation: In Hangul, • is Sky/Sun, ㅡ is Earth/Ground, and ㅣ is the upright standing Person!

questions.prompt: Which vowel starts the Korean word '오이' (Oi - Cucumber)?
questions.explanation: 오이 starts with ㅗ ('o')!

questions.prompt: Trace the vowel ㅏ (Ah) with your finger on the screen!
questions.explanation: Splendid! Vertical line first from top to bottom, then the middle short stroke to the right.

questions.prompt: Trace the vowel ㅗ (Oh) with your finger on the screen!
questions.explanation: Well done! Short top vertical stroke first, then the long horizontal base line.

title: Unit 3: Syllable Blocks (가, 나, 다, 라)
subtitle: Combining Consonant + Vowel
description: In Korean, letters snap together into cute syllable boxes like LEGO blocks!

lessons.title: Building Blocks: ㄱ + ㅏ = 가
lessons.introduction: Watch magic happen: snap consonant 'ㄱ' and vowel 'ㅏ' side-by-side to make '가' (Ga)!

cards.mnemonic: ㄱ (g) + ㅏ (a) = 가 (ga). Means 'Go'!
ㄴ (n) + ㅏ (a) = 나 (na). Means 'I' or 'Me'!

storyPages.text: Baby Bear packed his bag to go: '가' (Ga)!
He pointed happily at himself: '나' (Na - Me)!

lessons.title: Building Blocks: ㄷ + ㅏ = 다 & ㄹ + ㅏ = 라
lessons.introduction: Let's finish the famous Korean 'Ga-Na-Da-Ra' song by snapping ㄷ and ㄹ with ㅏ!

cards.mnemonic: ㄷ (d) + ㅏ (a) = 다 (da). Means 'All' or 'Everything'!
ㄹ (r/l) + ㅏ (a) = 라 (ra/la). Like singing 'La-la-la'!

storyPages.text: Baby Bear opened the door and shouted 'All together!': '다' (Da)!
He skipped down the road singing a happy tune: '라' (Ra/La)!
Now he can sing the Korean ABCs: 가, 나, 다, 라 (Ga, Na, Da, Ra)!

questions.prompt: What syllable do you get when you combine 'ㄱ' (g) and 'ㅏ' (a)?
questions.explanation: ㄱ + ㅏ = 가 (Ga)!

questions.prompt: What does the syllable '나' (ㄴ + ㅏ) mean in Korean?
questions.explanation: 나 (Na) is the Korean word for 'I' or 'Me'!

questions.prompt: Which syllable block combines the consonant 'ㄷ' (d) and vowel 'ㅏ' (a)?
questions.explanation: ㄷ + ㅏ snaps together to form '다' (Da)!

questions.prompt: Listen to the syllable sound and choose the matching block:
questions.explanation: You heard '가' (Ga)!

questions.prompt: Listen to the audio. Which syllable block is being spoken?
questions.explanation: You heard '나' (Na)!

questions.prompt: Combine 'ㄹ' (r/l) and 'ㅏ' (a). Which syllable is formed?
questions.explanation: ㄹ + ㅏ combines into '라' (Ra/La)!

questions.prompt: The word '가방' (bag) begins with which syllable block?
questions.explanation: 가방 (bag) starts with 가 (ga)!

questions.prompt: The word '나무' (tree) begins with which syllable block?
questions.explanation: 나무 (tree) starts with 나 (na)!

questions.prompt: Trace the syllable block 가 (Ga) with your finger!
questions.explanation: Brilliant! You wrote consonant ㄱ on the left, and vowel ㅏ on the right!

questions.prompt: Trace the syllable block 나 (Na) with your finger!
questions.explanation: Outstanding! ㄴ sits on the left and ㅏ stands on the right to form 나!

title: Unit 4: Everyday Consonants (ㅁ, ㅂ, ㅅ, ㅇ, ㅈ)
subtitle: Mouth, Bucket, Mountain & the Magic Circle
description: Learn the next 5 essential consonants, including the silent circle 'ㅇ' used in almost every Korean sentence!

lessons.title: Meet ㅁ (Mieum) & ㅂ (Bieup)
lessons.introduction: These two letters are made with your lips! Look at their boxy shapes.

cards.mnemonic: A square box that looks just like an open Mouth! Makes the 'm' sound as in 'mom'.
Looks like a Bucket half-filled with water! Makes a soft 'b' sound as in 'bucket'.

storyPages.text: Baby Bear carried a wooden Bucket 'ㅂ' (b) into the sunny meadow.
He opened his square Mouth 'ㅁ' (m) wide to taste a sweet berry: 'Mmm!'

lessons.title: Meet ㅅ (Siot), ㅇ (Ieung) & ㅈ (Jieut)
lessons.introduction: Meet the Mountain, the Silent Circle, and the Jar! Tip: 'ㅇ' is silent at the start of a block, and 'ng' at the bottom.

cards.mnemonic: Two strokes leaning together like a Ski mountain peak! Makes a gentle 's' sound as in 'sun' (or 'sh' before 'i').
Looks like a Zero (0)! At the start of a block it makes ZERO sound (silent placeholder, like 아 = 'a'). At the bottom, it rings like 'ng' in 'sing'!
A mountain 'ㅅ' with a lid on top like a Jar! Makes a soft 'j' sound as in 'jam'.

story.title: The Silent Ring on the Mountain

storyPages.text: Baby Bear climbed up the steep Ski mountain peak: 'ㅅ' (s)!
At the top, the golden sun looked like a round silent Ring: 'ㅇ'!
He jumped for Joy with a flat roof over his head: 'ㅈ' (j)!

questions.prompt: Which consonant looks like a square Mouth and makes the 'm' sound?
questions.explanation: ㅁ (Mieum) is shaped like an open Mouth and makes the 'm' sound!

questions.prompt: Which consonant looks like a Bucket half-full of water ('b')?
questions.explanation: ㅂ (Bieup) looks like a Bucket and makes the 'b' sound!

questions.prompt: What sound does 'ㅇ' make when it sits at the START (left/top) of a syllable block like '아'?
questions.explanation: Think of ㅇ as Zero (0)! At the start of a syllable block, it is a silent placeholder so the vowel can stand in a block.

questions.prompt: Which consonant looks like a Ski mountain peak and makes the 's' sound?
questions.explanation: ㅅ (Siot) has two strokes meeting like a mountain peak and makes the 's' sound!

questions.prompt: Which consonant starts the Korean word '바나나' (Banana)?
questions.explanation: 바나나 starts with 바 (ㅂ + ㅏ), using the Bucket letter 'ㅂ' (b)!

questions.prompt: Listen to the syllable '마' (Ma). Which consonant is at the start?
questions.explanation: 마 (Ma) starts with ㅁ (m)!

questions.prompt: Listen to the word '사과' (Sagwa - Apple). Which consonant does it start with?
questions.explanation: 사과 starts with 사 (ㅅ + ㅏ), which uses 'ㅅ' (s)!

questions.prompt: If 'ㅏ' is 'a', how do we write the syllable '아' (a) properly as a complete Korean block?
questions.explanation: Vowels never stand alone in Korean words! Silent 'ㅇ' + 'ㅏ' = '아' (a).

questions.prompt: Trace the square Mouth letter ㅁ (Mieum) with your finger!
questions.explanation: Great job! ㅁ is drawn with a left vertical line, top-right corner, and bottom closing bar.

questions.prompt: Trace the mountain letter ㅅ (Siot) with your finger!
questions.explanation: Awesome! ㅅ starts with a left-curving slope from the top, then a right-leaning support stroke.

title: Unit 5: Puffy Air Consonants (ㅊ, ㅋ, ㅌ, ㅍ, ㅎ)
subtitle: Upgrading Letters with a Puff of Air
description: Add one extra stroke to letters you already know to create airy, aspirated sounds!

lessons.title: Airy Upgrades: ㅋ (k), ㅌ (t) & ㅍ (p)
lessons.introduction: Hold your hand in front of your mouth! Adding a line to ㄱ, ㄷ, and ㅂ gives them a strong puff of air.

cards.mnemonic: It's 'ㄱ' (g) with an extra line, looking like an old Key! Makes a strong, breathy 'k' sound as in 'key'. (Koreans type ㅋㅋㅋ for 'hahaha'!)
It's 'ㄷ' (d) with a middle bar—looks like a capital 'E' or Teeth! Makes a breathy 't' sound as in 'top'.
Looks like two Pillars with a roof and floor (Roman numeral II)! Upgrades 'b' into a puffy 'p' sound as in 'pop'.

storyPages.text: A windy breeze blew through the forest, turning 'ㄱ' into a Key: 'ㅋ' (k)!
A little rabbit chattered its Teeth in the breeze: 'ㅌ' (t)!
Sweet purple grapes popped between two Pillars: 'ㅍ' (p)!

lessons.title: Hats On! ㅊ (ch) & ㅎ (h)
lessons.introduction: Put a cute little top-hat stroke on ㅈ (j) and ㅇ (silent) to get 'ch' and 'h'! With these two, you know ALL 14 basic consonants!

cards.mnemonic: It's 'ㅈ' (j) wearing a little chimney or antenna on top! Makes a crisp 'ch' sound as in 'cheer'.
A round head 'ㅇ' wearing a fancy Hat on top! Makes a happy 'h' sound as in 'hat' (ㅎㅎㅎ = 'hehehe').

storyPages.text: Baby Bear put a tall top-hat on his round head 'ㅇ' and laughed: 'ㅎ' (h - Ha ha)!
He sipped warm tea and cheered with his friends: 'ㅊ' (ch - Cha)!

questions.prompt: When you add an extra horizontal stroke to 'ㄱ' (g), which puffy 'k' letter do you get?
questions.explanation: ㄱ (g) upgrades into ㅋ (k)! Koreans also use ㅋㅋㅋ to mean 'hahaha' in text messages.

questions.prompt: Which letter looks like a round head 'ㅇ' wearing a Hat and makes the 'h' sound?
questions.explanation: ㅎ (Hieut) is a circle wearing a hat on top, making the 'h' sound!

questions.prompt: Which letter upgrades 'ㄷ' (d) into a breathy 't' sound (looking like a capital E)?
questions.explanation: ㅌ (Tieut) adds a middle stroke to ㄷ and makes the 't' sound!

questions.prompt: Which letter upgrades 'ㅈ' (j) by adding a little top stroke to make the 'ch' sound?
questions.explanation: ㅊ (Chieut) is ㅈ with a top stroke, making the 'ch' sound as in '차' (Cha - Tea/Car)!

questions.prompt: Which consonant looks like two pillars with a roof and floor, making the 'p' sound?
questions.explanation: ㅍ (Pieup) makes the 'p' sound as in '포도' (Podo - Grapes)!

questions.prompt: Listen to the word '코' (Ko - Nose). How is it written in Hangul?
questions.explanation: ㅋ (k) + ㅗ (o) = 코 (Ko - Nose)!

questions.prompt: Listen to the syllable '하' (Ha). Which block matches the sound?
questions.explanation: ㅎ (h) + ㅏ (a) = 하 (Ha)!

questions.prompt: What does the Korean word '차' (ㅊ + ㅏ) mean?
questions.explanation: 차 (Cha) means both 'Tea' and 'Car' in Korean!

questions.prompt: Trace the Key letter ㅋ (Kieuk) with your finger!
questions.explanation: Superb! Draw ㄱ first, then add the horizontal key stroke in the middle!

questions.prompt: Trace the E-shaped letter ㅌ (Tieut) with your finger!
questions.explanation: Great job! Top bar, middle bar, then the L-shaped bottom base!

title: Unit 6: Y-Vowels & E-Vowels (ㅑ, ㅕ, ㅛ, ㅠ, ㅐ, ㅔ)
subtitle: Double-Dash Magic & Everyday 'Eh' Vowels
description: Add one extra dash to basic vowels to add a 'Y' sound, and combine vowels to make 'ae' and 'e'!

lessons.title: The Y-Vowel Magic: ㅑ (ya), ㅕ (yeo), ㅛ (yo), ㅠ (yu)
lessons.introduction: Here is the easiest trick in Korean: add ONE extra short dash to ㅏ, ㅓ, ㅗ, or ㅜ, and a 'Y' sound jumps to the front!

cards.mnemonic: ㅏ (a) + 1 dash = ㅑ (ya)! Likewise, ㅓ (eo) + 1 dash = ㅕ (yeo as in 'young').
ㅗ (o) + 1 dash = ㅛ (yo)! ㅜ (u) + 1 dash = ㅠ (yu, which looks like crying eyes ㅠㅠ)!

storyPages.text: Baby Bear shouted to his friend across the field: '야!' (Ya - Hey)!
They cooked a delicious meal together: '요리' (Yori - Cooking)!
And drank fresh cold milk: '우유' (Uyu - Milk)!

lessons.title: The 'Eh' Twins: ㅐ (ae) & ㅔ (e)
lessons.introduction: When ㅏ or ㅓ holds hands with ㅣ (i), they form the 'Eh' twins: ㅐ (ae) and ㅔ (e)! In modern Seoul Korean, both sound like 'eh' in 'bed'.

cards.mnemonic: ㅏ (a) + ㅣ (i) = ㅐ (ae). The bridge is on the OUTSIDE right, looking like a capital 'H'! Sounds like 'eh' in 'care' or 'bed'.
ㅓ (eo) + ㅣ (i) = ㅔ (e). The short dash pokes out to the LEFT! Sounds like 'e' in 'yes' (네 = Ne = Yes!).

storyPages.text: Baby Bear met a friendly little Dog wagging its tail: '개' (Gae - Dog)!
The puppy barked 'Are we friends?' and Baby Bear nodded: '네!' (Ne - Yes)!

questions.prompt: What happens to the sound when you add ONE extra short stroke to ㅏ (a), ㅓ (eo), ㅗ (o), or ㅜ (u)?
options: It adds a 'Y' sound to the front (ya, yeo, yo, yu)
It adds an 'M' sound to the end
questions.explanation: Adding a second stroke adds a 'y' glide: ㅏ➔ㅑ(ya), ㅓ➔ㅕ(yeo), ㅗ➔ㅛ(yo), ㅜ➔ㅠ(yu)!

questions.prompt: Which vowel upgrades 'ㅗ' (o) into 'ㅛ' (yo)?
questions.explanation: ㅛ has two vertical strokes rising above the horizon line, making the 'yo' sound!

questions.prompt: In Korean text messages, which vowel looks like crying eyes ('T_T') and sounds like 'yu'?
questions.explanation: ㅠ (yu) has two downward strokes like teardrops, so Koreans type ㅠㅠ when crying!

questions.prompt: Which vowel combines ㅏ + ㅣ (looking like a capital H) to make the 'ae / eh' sound as in '개' (Dog)?
questions.explanation: ㅐ (ae) is formed from ㅏ + ㅣ with the horizontal bar in the middle like an 'H'!

questions.prompt: How do you write '네' (Ne - Yes) using ㄴ (n) and the vowel ㅔ (e)?
questions.explanation: ㄴ (n) + ㅔ (e) = 네 (Ne), the polite Korean word for 'Yes'!

questions.prompt: Listen to the word '우유' (Uyu - Milk). Which two vowels do you hear?
questions.explanation: 우유 (Uyu - Milk) uses ㅜ (u) in the first block and ㅠ (yu) in the second block!

questions.prompt: Listen to the word '개' (Gae - Dog). Choose the correct Hangul block:
questions.explanation: ㄱ (g) + ㅐ (ae) = 개 (Gae - Dog)!

questions.prompt: Match the vowel pair that sounds virtually identical ('eh') in modern everyday Korean:
questions.explanation: In modern spoken Korean, both ㅐ and ㅔ sound like a relaxed 'eh' (as in 'bed'), though we keep their distinct spellings!

questions.prompt: Trace the Y-vowel ㅑ (Ya) with your finger!
questions.explanation: Fantastic! Long vertical line first, followed by two short horizontal strokes to the right!

questions.prompt: Trace the vowel ㅐ (Ae) with your finger!
questions.explanation: Wonderful! Left vertical line, middle bridge stroke, then the right vertical line!

title: Unit 7: W-Vowels & Diphthongs (ㅘ, ㅝ, ㅚ, ㅟ, ㅢ)
subtitle: Gliding Two Vowels Together
description: Snap a bottom vowel and a side vowel together to make smooth 'Wa', 'Wo', 'We', and 'Wi' glides!

lessons.title: The 'W' Glides: ㅘ (wa) & ㅝ (wo)
lessons.introduction: When ㅗ (o) or ㅜ (u) slides quickly into ㅏ (a) or ㅓ (eo), your lips naturally make a 'W' sound! (Note: Bright ㅗ pairs with Bright ㅏ; Cozy ㅜ pairs with Cozy ㅓ!)

cards.mnemonic: Say 'o' + 'a' really fast: o-a, o-a... 'Wa'! In Korean, saying '와!' (Wa!) means 'Wow!'.
Say 'u' + 'eo' fast: u-eo... 'Wo' as in 'wonder'! Used in '고마워' (Gomawo - Thanks) and '뭐' (Mwo - What).

storyPages.text: Baby Bear saw a giant shiny red apple ('사과') and gasped: '와!' (Wa - Wow)!
Mama Bear handed it to him, and he smiled: '고마워요!' (Gomawoyo - Thank you)!

lessons.title: Smooth Combos: ㅟ (wi), ㅚ/ㅙ/ㅞ (we) & ㅢ (ui)
lessons.introduction: Let's meet the remaining vowel combinations! Once you know these, you can read EVERY vowel in the Korean language.

cards.mnemonic: Say 'oo' + 'ee' fast: 'Wi' (like English 'we')! With a silent ㅇ, '위' (Wi) means 'Up / Above'.
ㅡ (eu) + ㅣ (i) glides together into 'ui' (as in 의사 Uisa = Doctor)! Bonus: ㅚ, ㅙ, and ㅞ all sound like 'we' in 'wedding' (왜 Wae = Why?).

storyPages.text: Baby Bear looked UP at the tall tree branch: '위' (Wi - Up/Above)!
Kind Doctor Owl ('의사' - Uisa) asked 'Why ('왜' - Wae) are you climbing so high?'

questions.prompt: When you glide ㅗ (o) and ㅏ (a) together into 'ㅘ', what sound does it make?
questions.explanation: ㅗ (o) + ㅏ (a) glides smoothly into 'ㅘ' (wa)!

questions.prompt: Which two basic vowels combine to make 'ㅝ' (wo)?
questions.explanation: Cozy vowel ㅜ (u) and cozy vowel ㅓ (eo) combine to form ㅝ (wo)!

questions.prompt: What sound does 'ㅟ' (ㅜ + ㅣ) make, and what does '위' mean?
questions.explanation: ㅜ (u) + ㅣ (i) = ㅟ (wi), and '위' means 'Up' or 'On top'!

questions.prompt: Which compound vowel combines flat Earth 'ㅡ' and standing Person 'ㅣ' to start the word '의사' (Uisa - Doctor)?
questions.explanation: ㅡ (eu) + ㅣ (i) = ㅢ (ui), used in 의사 (Uisa - Doctor)!

questions.prompt: Listen to the exclamation '와!' (Wa! - Wow!). How is it written?
questions.explanation: Silent ㅇ + ㅘ (wa) = 와 (Wa - Wow)!

questions.prompt: Listen to the word '가위' (Gawi - Scissors). Which blocks do you hear?
questions.explanation: 가 (ga) + 위 (wi) = 가위 (Gawi - Scissors)!

questions.prompt: In the word '사과' (Sagwa - Apple), how is the second block '과' (gwa) built?
questions.explanation: ㄱ (g) + ㅘ (wa) snaps together into 과 (gwa)!

questions.prompt: Why does Korean never combine ㅗ (o) with ㅓ (eo)?
options: Because of Vowel Harmony: Bright ㅗ pairs with Bright ㅏ (ㅘ), and Cozy ㅜ pairs with Cozy ㅓ (ㅝ)!
questions.explanation: Korean follows Vowel Harmony! Bright vowels (ㅗ, ㅏ) stick together (ㅘ), and dark/cozy vowels (ㅜ, ㅓ) stick together (ㅝ).

questions.prompt: What do the compound vowels ㅚ, ㅙ, and ㅞ all sound like in modern Korean?
questions.explanation: In modern Seoul Korean, ㅚ, ㅙ, and ㅞ all converge to the 'we' sound!

questions.prompt: Listen to the friendly phrase '고마워요' (Gomawoyo - Thank you). Which W-vowel is in '워'?
questions.explanation: 고마워요 uses '워' (ㅇ + ㅝ), which has the ㅝ (wo) vowel!

title: Unit 8: Double (Tense) Consonants (ㄲ, ㄸ, ㅃ, ㅆ, ㅉ)
subtitle: Twin Letters with Crisp, Tight Energy!
description: Meet the 5 twin consonants! No puff of air—just tense your vocal cords for a crisp, popping sound.

lessons.title: Crisp Twins: ㄲ (kk), ㄸ (tt) & ㅃ (pp)
lessons.introduction: Now you know the 3-way Korean consonant trio: Soft (ㄱ, ㄷ, ㅂ), Airy (ㅋ, ㅌ, ㅍ), and Twin/Tense (ㄲ, ㄸ, ㅃ)! For twins, hold back the puff of air and pop the sound cleanly.

cards.mnemonic: Two ㄱ letters side by side! Sounds like the crisp, unaspirated 'k' in 'sky' or 'skill' (zero puff of air).
Two ㄷ doors side by side! Sounds like the crisp 't' in 'stop' or 'star'.
Two ㅂ buckets side by side! Press your lips tightly and pop them open like 'p' in 'spin' or 'spy'.

storyPages.text: A fluffy white Rabbit ('토끼' - Tokki) hopped by with a twitching tail!
Baby Bear picked sweet red Strawberries ('딸기' - Ttalgi) in the sunshine.
He shared fresh Bread ('빵') with his loving Dad ('아빠' - Appa)!

lessons.title: Sizzling Twins: ㅆ (ss) & ㅉ (jj)
lessons.introduction: Finish the entire Hangul alphabet with ㅆ (ss) and ㅉ (jj)! Once you finish this lesson, you know ALL 40 letters of Hangul!

cards.mnemonic: Two ㅅ mountains side by side! Whereas single ㅅ is a soft, relaxed 's', twin ㅆ is a sharp, hissing 'ss' as in 'hiss' or 'sun'!
Two ㅈ letters side by side! A tight, energetic 'jj' sound—used when Koreans say '짱!' (Jjang! = Awesome / The Best!).

storyPages.text: Mama Bear cooked a warm, bubbling pot of stew: '찌개' (Jjigae)!
Baby Bear cheered because he now knows all 40 letters of Hangul: '짱!' (Jjang - Awesome)!

questions.prompt: How are Korean double (tense) consonants like ㄲ, ㄸ, ㅃ pronounced compared to ㅋ, ㅌ, ㅍ?
options: Crisp and tense with ZERO puff of air (like 'k' in 'sky' or 'p' in 'spin')
With a huge puff of air
questions.explanation: Double consonants (쌍자음) are pronounced with tight vocal cords and no puff of air!

questions.prompt: Which word uses the twin consonant 'ㅃ' (pp) to mean 'Dad / Papa'?
questions.explanation: 아빠 (Appa) uses ㅃ (pp) and means 'Dad'!

questions.prompt: Which twin consonant starts the Korean word '딸기' (Ttalgi - Strawberry)?
questions.explanation: 딸기 (Strawberry) begins with ㄸ (tt)!

questions.prompt: Which twin consonant makes a sharp, hissing 'ss' sound as in '비싸요' (Bissayo - Expensive)?
questions.explanation: ㅆ (Ssang-siot) makes the sharp, tense 'ss' sound!

questions.prompt: Listen to the word '토끼' (Tokki - Rabbit). How is the second syllable written?
questions.explanation: 토끼 uses the tense twin consonant ㄲ + ㅣ = 끼 (kki)!

questions.prompt: Listen carefully to the contrast. Which syllable is being spoken: '사' (sa) or '싸' (ssa)?
questions.explanation: You heard the sharp, tense '싸' (ssa) with twin ㅆ!

questions.prompt: Compare the 3-way Korean consonant trio for G/K: Soft ➔ Airy ➔ Tense Twin:
options: ㄱ (soft g) ➔ ㅋ (airy k) ➔ ㄲ (tense kk)
questions.explanation: Korean organizes stops in 3-way trios: Soft (ㄱ, ㄷ, ㅂ, ㅈ), Airy (ㅋ, ㅌ, ㅍ, ㅊ), and Tense Twins (ㄲ, ㄸ, ㅃ, ㅉ)!

questions.prompt: What does the slang word '짱!' (Jjang - starting with ㅉ) mean in Korean?
questions.explanation: 짱 (Jjang) means 'Awesome!' or 'The Best!'—just like you for mastering all of Hangul!

questions.prompt: Trace the twin consonant ㄲ (Ssang-giyeok) with your finger!
questions.explanation: Awesome! Two neat ㄱ shapes side by side form ㄲ!

questions.prompt: Trace the twin consonant ㅆ (Ssang-siot) with your finger!
questions.explanation: Brilliant! Two mountain peaks side by side form ㅆ!

title: Unit 9: Final Consonants (Batchim) & Polite Phrases
subtitle: 3-Letter Blocks & Everyday Greetings
description: Put all 40 letters to work! Read 3-letter Batchim blocks (물, 밥, 빵) and speak your first polite Korean phrases!

lessons.title: The Floor Cushion (Batchim): 물 (Water), 밥 (Rice) & 빵 (Bread)
lessons.introduction: When a 3rd consonant sits on the floor at the bottom of a syllable block, Koreans call it 'Batchim' (support cushion)!

cards.mnemonic: ㅁ (m) on top + ㅜ (u) in the middle + ㄹ (l) on the floor = 물 (mul). Essential word for 'Water'!
ㅂ (b) + ㅏ (a) on top, with ㅂ (p) sitting at the bottom = 밥 (bap). Means 'Rice' or 'Meal'!
Twin ㅃ (pp) + ㅏ (a) on top, with circle ㅇ ('ng') on the floor = 빵 (ppang - Bread)!

storyPages.text: Baby Bear opened his lunchbox to eat warm Rice ('밥' - Bap) and soft Bread ('빵' - Ppang)!
And he drank cool, fresh spring Water: '물' (Mul)!

lessons.title: Polite Greetings: Hello, Thank You & Please
lessons.introduction: In Korean culture, adding '-요' (yo) or '-니다' (nida) at the end makes your words polite and warm. Let's speak real Korean!

cards.mnemonic: Literally asks 'Are you at peace?'. Say 'Annyeong' to close friends, and 'Annyeong-haseyo' to be polite to anyone!
감사 (Gamsa = Gratitude) + 합니다 (hamnida = I do). Pronunciation tip: The 'ㅂ' in 합 meets 'ㄴ' and sounds softly like 'm' (Gam-sa-ham-ni-da)!
Put any item in front of '주세요' (Juseyo) to order politely! 물 주세요 (Mul juseyo) = 'Water, please!'

story.title: Baby Bear Visits the Forest Cafe

storyPages.text: Baby Bear bowed politely to Wise Owl and said Hello: '안녕하세요' (Annyeong-haseyo)!
He ordered politely: '물 주세요!' (Mul juseyo - Water, please)!
Baby Bear received the cup with both paws and said: '감사합니다!' (Gamsa-hamnida - Thank you)!

questions.prompt: What do Koreans call the final consonant that sits at the bottom of a syllable block (like 'ㄹ' in '물')?
questions.explanation: Batchim (받침) means 'support' or 'floor cushion'—it's the final consonant at the bottom of a syllable block!

questions.prompt: What does the 3-letter Korean word '물' (ㅁ + ㅜ + ㄹ, mul) mean?
questions.explanation: 물 (mul) means 'Water'!

questions.prompt: In the word '빵' (Ppang - Bread), what sound does the circle 'ㅇ' make at the BOTTOM of the block?
questions.explanation: While ㅇ is silent at the top/left of a block, as a bottom Batchim it makes the ringing 'ng' sound: ㅃ + ㅏ + ㅇ = 빵 (ppang)!

questions.prompt: How do you say a polite 'Hello' to someone in Korean?
questions.explanation: 안녕하세요 (Annyeong-haseyo) is the standard polite way to say 'Hello'!

questions.prompt: Which expression means 'Thank you' politely in Korean?
questions.explanation: 감사합니다 (Gamsa-hamnida) means 'Thank you'!

questions.prompt: Listen carefully to the phrase. What is the speaker asking for?
questions.explanation: You heard '물 주세요' (Mul juseyo), which means 'Water, please'!

questions.prompt: Listen to the greeting. Which phrase did you hear?
questions.explanation: You heard '안녕하세요' (Annyeong-haseyo - Hello)!

questions.prompt: How do you politely ask for cooked rice ('밥') at a Korean restaurant?
questions.explanation: Noun + 주세요 (juseyo) means 'Please give me [Noun]', so '밥 주세요' means 'Rice, please!'.

questions.prompt: Trace the 3-letter Batchim block 산 (San - Mountain) with your finger!
questions.explanation: Amazing! You wrote ㅅ + ㅏ on top and tucked the Batchim ㄴ underneath to make 산!

questions.prompt: In '감사합니다' (Thank you), why is '합니다' pronounced 'ham-ni-da' instead of 'hap-ni-da'?
options: Because ㅂ (p) softens to an 'm' sound before ㄴ (n) for smooth pronunciation
questions.explanation: In Korean, when Batchim ㅂ meets ㄴ right after it, ㅂ nasalizes into 'm' so your mouth can flow smoothly: Gam-sa-ham-ni-da!
